title: Understanding vs. Generation: Navigating Optimization Dilemma in Multimodal Models
claim: Training on one capability degrades the other and naive co-training barely helps, while our method improves both together.
layout: single grouped bar chart, five conditions left-to-right, dashed baseline reference lines
description: A single grouped bar chart with accuracy (%) on the y-axis, running from 20 to 100. Five conditions sit along the x-axis: Initial, Gen✓, Und✓, Gen+Und✓ and Ours. Each condition has two bars: peach for Generation ACC and light blue for Understanding ACC. Bold numeric labels sit above every bar. Two dashed horizontal lines, peach and blue, extend from the Initial bars across the whole plot as baselines. Generation-only training raises generation to 57.5 but lowers understanding to 79.8. Understanding-only training raises understanding to 82.4 but drops generation to 32.5. Naive co-training barely moves either bar (50.0 and 80.7). The Ours group jumps to 80.0 for generation and 85.9 for understanding, well above both dashed lines. The legend is in the top-left corner. The eye goes first to the tall Ours bars at the right.
caption: Fine-tuning BAGEL exclusively on generation or understanding degrades the complementary capability. Naive co-training shows minor gains, whereas our proposed method demonstrates significant improvement in both. Results are reported on counting subset of GenEval++.
abstract: Current research in multimodal models faces a key challenge where enhancing generative capabilities often comes at the expense of understanding, and vice versa. We analyzed this trade-off and identify the primary cause might be the potential conflict between generation and understanding, which creates a competitive dynamic within the model. To address this, we propose the Reason-Reflect-Refine (R3) framework. This innovative algorithm re-frames the single-step generation task into a multi-step process of "generate-understand-regenerate". By explicitly leveraging the model's understanding capability during generation, we successfully mitigate the optimization dilemma, achieved stronger generation results and improved understanding ability which are related to the generation process. This offers valuable insights for designing next-generation unified multimodal models. Code is available at https://github.com/sen-ye/R3.
